title: strategy_analyzer.R IC/FMB/Liquidity Loop Performance Optimization
author: Architect
trigger: Session 69 Day 1 — STR_1689/STR_1686 Step 6 timeout (90s limit hit)

diagnosis.symptom: run_analysis() exceeds 90s setTimeLimit, producing '[Step 6 WARN] reached elapsed time limit' and skipping IC/FMB/Rolling/Stress/Liquidity outputs entirely.
diagnosis.impact: analysis_ic.csv, analysis_fmb.csv, analysis_rolling.csv not generated => S6 cascade Gate missing IC/ICIR/FMB material

root_causes.description: all_dates <- sort(unique(RAWDATA$Date)) called INSIDE the for-loop. RAWDATA has 14.17M rows. sort(unique()) on 14.17M Date values costs ~0.3s per call. Over 268 iterations = ~80s on this single line alone.
root_causes.complexity: O(N_signal * M_rawdata) where N_signal=268, M_rawdata=14.17M. The sort(unique()) is O(M log M) repeated N times = O(N * M log M)

root_causes.description: RAWDATA[Date >= exec_d & Date <= next_exec & Ticker %in% fac$Ticker, ...] performs a full table scan on 14.17M rows (no key set). Each iteration scans ~14M rows for a range filter + Ticker membership test. Over 268 iterations = ~268 * 14M row comparisons.

root_causes.location: Lines 112-153 — FMB loop duplicates IC loop structure
root_causes.description: FMB loop repeats the same pattern with 3 additional RAWDATA subsets per iteration (rets, size_dt, mom_dt). Although all_dates_fmb is hoisted outside the loop (line 110), the 3 unkeyed RAWDATA subsets (lines 122, 126, 129) scan 14M rows each = 3 * 268 * 14M row comparisons.

RAWDATA[Ticker %in% tickers & Date <= sd_date][order(Date), tail(.SD, 20), by = Ticker] performs full scan + sort + group-tail. With 268 signal dates and 14M rows, this adds significant time. The order() + tail(.SD, 20) pattern is O(M log M) per iteration.

root_causes.location: Missing — no setkey() on RAWDATA or FACTORS
root_causes.description: RAWDATA loaded from parquet via as.data.table(read_parquet()) loses all keys. data.table subset operations (Date ==, Date >=, Ticker %in%) fall back to vector scan instead of binary search. Setting key(RAWDATA, Date, Ticker) would convert O(M) scans to O(log M) lookups.
root_causes.complexity: Every subset degrades from O(log M) to O(M)

estimated_current_time.observed: 90s timeout hit before IC loop completes

options.name: data.table vectorization + key + hoist
options.description: Pure R/data.table optimization: (1) setkey(RAWDATA, Date, Ticker) at entry, (2) hoist all_dates outside loop, (3) pre-compute period returns as a single vectorized operation, (4) replace IC loop with by=sig_date group operation
options.regression_risk: LOW — same algorithm, same output schema, just vectorized
options.pit_risk: NONE — no change to data access pattern or temporal logic

details.step1_key: setkey(RAWDATA, Date, Ticker) — O(M log M) once, saves O(M) per subset
details.step2_hoist: Move sort(unique(RAWDATA$Date)) to line 64 (before loop). One-time cost: 0.3s vs 80s.
details.step3_period_rets: Pre-join FACTORS with RAWDATA and compute period returns via data.table grouped operation instead of 268 separate subsets
details.step4_ic_vectorize: Use FACTORS[, sig_idx := .GRP, by=Date] then merge with RAWDATA period returns, compute cor() by sig_idx group

options.name: Option A + parallel::mclapply for FMB lm()
options.description: Apply Option A vectorization for IC loop, then parallelize FMB regressions with mclapply (lm() is the non-vectorizable part). WSL typically has 4+ cores available.
options.regression_risk: LOW — mclapply preserves determinism (same seed per chunk)
options.pit_risk: NONE — parallelism doesn't change data access temporal logic

details.parallel_scope: FMB lm() fitting only (268 independent regressions)
details.overhead: mclapply fork cost ~0.5s, negligible vs 120s savings

options.name: Rcpp inner loop (period return computation)
options.description: Move the period return computation (prod(1+Ret) over date range by Ticker) to C++ via Rcpp. This is the innermost hot loop.
options.estimated_speedup: 50-100x for the return computation kernel (but diminishing returns — Option A already removes the main bottleneck)
options.lines_changed: ~30 R lines + ~80 C++ lines in hurdle_gate_perf.cpp
options.regression_risk: MEDIUM — new C++ code requires careful testing for edge cases (NA handling, empty groups)
options.pit_risk: NONE — same temporal logic in C++

details.function: period_ret_by_ticker_cpp(dates, tickers, rets, date_from, date_to, target_tickers) -> data.table(Ticker, Period_Ret)
details.integration: Add to existing hurdle_gate_perf.cpp, fallback to R if Rcpp unavailable

options.name: Hybrid: A (vectorize) + C (Rcpp period_ret kernel) + incremental FMB
options.description: Full optimization stack: vectorized IC via data.table grouping, Rcpp for inner period_ret, and incremental (non-redundant) FMB data preparation.
options.regression_risk: MEDIUM — complex refactor requires thorough regression test

details.note: Marginal benefit over Option A is small. Recommended only if Option A proves insufficient.

recommendation.rationale: Option A eliminates 95%+ of the bottleneck with minimal code change and zero regression risk. The dominant cost is RC-1 (sort(unique) inside loop = 80s) and RC-5 (missing key = 2-5x slowdown on every subset). Fixing these two alone should bring total time from 300s+ to under 15s. The vectorized IC computation is a natural data.table idiom. Option B (mclapply) is a good follow-up if FMB still takes >10s after A, but is unlikely needed.
recommendation.fallback: If Option A does not achieve < 30s target, add Option B (mclapply for FMB) as incremental improvement.
recommendation.reject_reason_for_C_D: Rcpp (Option C/D) adds build complexity, C++ maintenance burden, and Rcpp compilation dependency. Given that Option A should achieve 15-30x speedup (well within 90s budget), the marginal gain does not justify the complexity.

option_A_diff.description: Detailed code changes for Option A — Forge implements exactly this spec

changes.section: Entry point (after line 60, before IC loop)
code: # --- Performance: key RAWDATA and pre-compute date vector ---
all_dates <- sort(unique(RAWDATA$Date))  # HOIST: once, not 268 times

changes.section: IC loop (lines 62-93) — REPLACE with vectorized version
changes.action: REPLACE entire for-loop with data.table group operation
changes.new_code_description: 1. Build a date mapping: for each signal_date, find exec_d and next_exec via binary search on all_dates. 2. Build a long table of (sig_date, Ticker, Score, Period_Ret) by joining FACTORS with RAWDATA period returns. 3. Compute IC = cor(rank(Score), rank(Period_Ret)) by sig_date group. All done without for-loop.
pseudocode: date_map[, exec_d := all_dates[findInterval(sig_date, all_dates) + 1L]]  # first date > sig_date
# 2. Pre-compute all period returns in one pass
# For each signal period i, we need prod(1+Ret) for Ticker where Date in [exec_d[i], next_exec[i]]
# Strategy: use non-equi join or foverlaps
RAWDATA_sub <- RAWDATA[, .(Date, Ticker, Ret)]  # minimal columns
# Non-equi join: RAWDATA_sub[date_map, on=.(Date >= exec_d, Date <= next_exec), allow.cartesian=TRUE]
period_rets <- RAWDATA_sub[date_map, on=.(Date >= exec_d, Date <= next_exec),
period_rets <- period_rets[, .(Period_Ret = prod(1 + Ret, na.rm=TRUE) - 1), by=.(sig_date, Ticker)]
# 3. Merge with FACTORS and compute IC
# Filter: minimum 10 stocks per signal date

changes.section: FMB loop (lines 109-154) — partial vectorize + retain lm() loop
changes.action: Vectorize data preparation, keep lm() in loop (lm is inherently sequential per-period)
changes: Pre-compute size_at_signal and mom_12m as single vectorized passes
Keep lm() fitting in loop but on pre-joined data

changes.action: DELETE: all_dates <- sort(unique(RAWDATA$Date)) from inside loop
changes.reason: This single line is ~80s of the ~300s total. Moving it outside the loop is the single highest-impact fix.

changes.action: Replace per-signal-date loop with rolling window join
changes: Pre-compute 20-day rolling average volume for all tickers
Join with hold_log by (Signal_Date, Ticker) to get volume at each signal date

regression_test.reason: Production PG2 strategy with known IC/ICIR/FMB values
regression_test.method: Run original code -> save analysis_ic.csv + analysis_fmb.csv. Run patched code -> compare. Max allowed delta: IC values within 1e-10 (floating point).

performance_benchmark.code: t0 <- proc.time(); run_analysis(sim, FACTORS, RAWDATA, BM_DT, OUT_DIR, 'benchmark'); elapsed <- (proc.time() - t0)[3]; cat(sprintf('Elapsed: %.1fs\n', elapsed))

edge_cases: FACTORS with < 10 stocks on some dates (should produce NA IC, same as before)
RAWDATA with Date gaps (missing trading days — should not affect results)
Empty hold_log (liquidity audit should skip gracefully)

l_code_draft.title: strategy_analyzer IC/FMB loop 10min+ timeout — sort(unique()) inside loop + missing setkey
l_code_draft.lesson_text: strategy_analyzer.R의 IC/FMB 계산 루프가 RAWDATA 14M rows에서 10분+ 소요되어 90s timeout에 걸림. 원인 3가지: (1) sort(unique(RAWDATA$Date))가 for-loop 내부에서 268회 반복 호출 (~80s), (2) RAWDATA에 setkey() 미설정으로 모든 subset이 vector scan (~2-5x 패널티), (3) IC/FMB의 RAWDATA subset이 268회 전체 테이블 스캔. 해결: all_dates 루프 밖 호이스트 + setkey(Date, Ticker) + 가능 시 data.table 그룹 연산 벡터화. 예상 15-30x 개선.
l_code_draft.core_reference: L-534 (루프 내 parquet 반복 로드 금지 — 동일 반패턴), CLAUDE.md data.table 키 규칙
